title: Open daily
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The shack goes to summer hours: open daily. Gully paints OPEN DAILY on a board and hangs it under the derby sign. The uncle says nobody's ever come daily. Gully says then it's for the sign's sake. The uncle lets it hang.

panels.composition: The shack. GULLY hanging a fresh board under the derby sign: OPEN DAILY in his blocky hand. The UNCLE on his pot. WOOD, BARNABY.

image.prompt: a stocky teenager hanging a hand-painted board beneath a crab sign on a shingle shack while an old man watches from a crab pot, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The board. Gully's letters. Uneven, committed.

image.prompt: close on a hand-painted wooden board with uneven committed block letters, black and white, no words

balloons.text: Then it's for the sign's sake.

image.prompt: an old weathered man, flat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The shack from the launch with two signs now. The dog under the new one. The strip counts signs the way it counts letters.

image.prompt: a shingle bait shack with two hand-painted signs stacked on its wall and a small dog lying beneath them, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Let it hang.' Two signs. The strip counts signs.
